newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty calm ahead of expected rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty calm ahead of expected rate rise.

text.p: The Polish zloty held flat around -1.3 percent from parity in early Friday trade and the market was expected to remain calm at least until interest rates increased, which dealers said could come as early as today.
"The situation will be peaceful at least until the official (interest rate rise) news appears," said Wojciech Czajkowski, forex dealer at Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA.

The National Bank of Poland, whose decision-making board meets on Friday, is widely expected to increase official rates, now at 22 and 25 percent for the discount and lombard, by one to two points. It may also up obligatory reserve requirements.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was at -1.25/-1.32 percent from the trading band centre against opening's -1.25/-1.34 percent.
It was at 3.4760/80 to the dollar and at 1.8815/30 to the mark versus 3.4765/80 and 1.8820/45 at opening respectively.

Analysts did not expect large foreign capital inflows after the pending rate rise because Poland's gaping current account deficit and uncertainty over upcoming parliamentary elections would likely continue to create downward pressure on the zloty.
They said however that shorter-term currency speculators may be attracted to Poland if treasury yields rose following the official rate increase.

At the daily WIBOR fixing at 0900 GMT all terms longer than tomorrow/next deposits were offered above the present lombard rate of 25 percent. One-month depos were at 24.30/26.20 percent, up more than a point from Thursday, while three- and six-month depos were offered at 26.42 percent.
On the market one-day rates eased slightly with overnight deposits at 24.15/24.55 percent at 0910 GMT, against opening's 24.25/24.55 and T/N at 24.30/24.75 against 24.35/24.85.
